theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: At work, what is a "familiar" problem?
options: A problem that only a manager is allowed to deal with
A problem of a kind that often comes up in your job
A problem that has never happened anywhere before
A problem that a guest causes on purpose to get money

questions.stem: Which of these is a familiar problem for a room attendant at a villa?
options: A hurricane tears the roof off the villa
The owner decides to sell the villa
The vacuum cleaner stops working mid-room
A film crew asks to use the villa for a movie

questions.stem: Why should a small problem, such as a dripping tap in a guest bathroom, be dealt with early?
options: So that you can show the guest how busy you are
Because a dripping tap is a serious danger to life
So that the guest will pay for the repair later
Small problems can grow, cost more and upset guests

questions.stem: What is the first step in solving a workplace problem?
options: Choose the quickest fix you can think of
Find out who caused it so they can be blamed
Write the problem in the report book
Work out clearly what the problem is

questions.stem: Why do you ask "what, where, when, who and how" questions about a problem?
options: To get the facts before you decide what to do
To make the problem look bigger than it is
To find a reason to pass the job to someone else
To fill in time until the supervisor arrives

questions.stem: Every afternoon the walk-in chiller at a restaurant in Kingston gets warm, so staff move the food to another fridge. Nobody reports the chiller. What are they doing?
options: Fixing the cause, so it will not happen again
Treating the sign of the problem, not its cause
Following the food safety procedure in full
Solving the problem in the best possible way

questions.stem: Guests at a villa in Negril say the hot water runs out each morning. Which question will best help to find the cause?
options: Which guest complained first, and how loudly?
When does it run out, and how many showers are taken then?
Can the guests take cold showers instead?
Did the guests complain at their last hotel?

questions.stem: Shanice, a room attendant, sees a spark when she turns on a light switch in a guest room. What should she do?
options: Open the switch plate and check the wires herself
Put tape over the switch and carry on cleaning
Stop using it, keep people away and report it
Leave it alone, since the light still comes on

questions.stem: What does it mean to work "within your authority"?
options: Doing whatever the guest asks, whatever the rules say
Doing any job, as long as you finish it quickly
Doing what a co-worker tells you to do
Doing only what your job role and rules allow

questions.stem: When should you pass a problem on to your supervisor instead of solving it yourself?
options: When it is unsafe or outside your role or skills
Only when a guest has asked to see the manager
Whenever you would rather not deal with it yourself
Never, because it shows that you cannot cope

questions.stem: When you report a problem to your supervisor, what should you tell them?
options: Only that there is a problem, and nothing more
What happened, where, when and what you have done
Who you think is to blame, and why they did it
How annoyed you feel about the person who caused it

questions.stem: Why should a problem be written down as well as reported by word of mouth?
options: So there is a record to check and follow up
So that the supervisor does not have to listen to you
Because spoken reports are against the law in Jamaica
So that you can prove the problem was not your fault

questions.stem: A bartender at a hotel in Montego Bay finds that the ice machine is leaking water onto the floor. Who should get the repair request?
options: The front office team at reception
The maintenance (engineering) team
The head chef in the main kitchen
The security guard at the gate

questions.stem: Why is it useful to think of more than one possible solution to a problem?
options: So that you can choose the one that works best
So that the job takes longer and you get overtime
So that you can try all of them at the same time
So that someone else can choose for you later

questions.stem: You and your supervisor have agreed on a solution. What should you do next?
options: Carry it out as agreed and follow the procedures
Wait until the problem happens again, then act
Change it to your own idea without telling anyone
Tell the guests about it and ask them to vote on it

questions.stem: Breakfast at a villa is often late because the bread is delivered at 8 a.m. Which is the best solution to suggest?
options: Tell guests that breakfast will now start at 10 a.m.
Serve breakfast with no bread until the van comes
Send a co-worker by taxi to buy bread each morning
Ask the bakery to deliver earlier, such as by 6 a.m.

questions.stem: When you compare possible solutions, which things should you weigh up?
options: Who suggested it, and how senior that person is
Safety, cost, time and the effect on guests
How new it is, and whether it looks modern
Whether it will give you less work to do

questions.stem: Tashana is setting up a wedding on a hotel lawn in Ocho Rios when heavy rain starts. The back-up plan is the covered terrace. What should she do?
options: Keep setting up on the lawn and hope the rain stops
Go home, since the wedding cannot go ahead
Follow plan B and move the set-up to the terrace
Cover the guests' chairs with towels and carry on

questions.stem: The till (point-of-sale) system at a restaurant stops working at lunch time. What is the best short-term action?
options: Close the restaurant until the system is repaired
Let guests leave without paying, to be kind
Use the back-up paper bills and report the fault
Guess each bill total and hope it is right

questions.stem: A tour bus taking visitors to an attraction in St Ann breaks down on the road. What should the tour guide do first?
options: Make sure the guests are safe, then call the office
Walk ahead alone to the attraction to fetch help
Ask the guests to help push the bus off the road
Leave the guests with the driver and take a taxi home

questions.stem: A guest slips on a wet patch beside the villa pool. What should you do first?
options: Mop the floor before anyone else slips on it
See if the guest is hurt and get first aid if needed
Ask the guest to sign a form saying it was their fault
Tell the guest the pool area is used at their own risk

questions.stem: You see cooking oil spilled on the kitchen floor during service. What should you do?
options: Walk round it and tell the dishwasher at the end of the shift
Throw a cloth over it and carry on with your work
Leave it, as oil dries quickly in a hot kitchen
Put a wet floor sign out and clean it up straight away

questions.stem: Boxes from a delivery are blocking the fire exit at the back of the restaurant. What is the right action?
options: Leave them, as the front door can be used instead
Clear the exit at once and tell the supervisor
Put a sign on the boxes saying "Fire exit"
Wait for the delivery driver to come back for them

questions.stem: A pan of oil catches fire on the stove in a villa kitchen. Which action is safe?
options: Throw a jug of water onto the burning pan
Carry the pan outside as fast as you can
Fan the flames with a towel to put them out
Turn off the heat and cover it with a fire blanket

questions.stem: The cable of a vacuum cleaner is cut and the wires show. What should the room attendant do?
options: Wrap the cut with tape and keep using it
Stop using it, label it faulty and report it
Use it only in rooms where there are no guests
Put it back in the store for the next shift

questions.stem: Why should faulty equipment be labelled "Do not use"?
options: So that it can be sold off at a good price
So that guests can see which items are old
So that the supervisor knows who broke it last
So that nobody uses it before it is repaired

questions.stem: Guests arrive at a villa at 11 a.m., but check-in is at 3 p.m. and their room is not ready. What is a good response?
options: Tell them to come back at 3 p.m. and close the door
Offer a drink and a place to wait, and say when
Give them the room as it is, before it is cleaned
Ask them why they did not read the check-in time

questions.stem: A hotel guest has lost his room key card. What must the front desk do before making a new one?
options: Check the guest's ID against the booking
Charge the guest for a new lock on the door
Ask the guest to search the beach for it first
Give the new card to whoever asks for it

questions.stem: A guest tells a server that she has a peanut allergy. The server is not sure whether a dish has nuts in it. What should the server do?
options: Say the dish is probably fine and serve it
Tell her to pick the nuts out if she finds any
Advise her to eat a small amount to test it
Check with the chef before the guest orders it

questions.stem: A guest at a beach bar has had too much to drink and is getting rude. What should the bartender do?
options: Give him one more free drink so that he calms down
Argue with him so that the other guests can see
Stay calm, stop serving him and call a supervisor
Ask some other guests to walk him back to his room

questions.stem: Two co-workers at a hotel keep arguing about whose turn it is to restock the bar. What is the best first step?
options: Ignore it, as it is not a problem for the guests
Take sides with the one who is your friend
Talk calmly and agree a fair schedule for it
Complain loudly about both of them to the guests

questions.stem: A co-worker is often late, so you keep doing extra work. What should you do first?
options: Speak to the co-worker politely about it
Start coming late yourself to make it fair
Post about it on social media after work
Stop doing any of your own work until they arrive

questions.stem: A new kitchen porter does not know how to use the dishwasher safely. What is the best way to help?
options: Let him work it out alone, by trial and error
Do all his washing for him for the rest of the week
Show him the steps, or ask the supervisor to train him
Tell him to watch a video on his phone during service

questions.stem: Why should you check the result after a solution has been carried out?
options: To make sure the problem is really fixed
To find something new to complain about
To prove that the supervisor was wrong
To use up the time left in your shift

questions.stem: Maintenance has repaired the air conditioner in a villa bedroom. How can the room attendant check the repair?
options: Wait for the next guest to say if it works
Look at it and see if it looks new
Switch it on and check the room cools
Read the repair note and trust it

questions.stem: You tried a solution, but the problem has come back. What should you do?
options: Give up, because this problem cannot be solved
Keep trying the same solution again and again
Look at it again and try another option
Hide the problem so that nobody else notices it

questions.stem: Why should problems be written in the property's log book?
options: So patterns can be seen and the problem prevented
So that staff can be fined for every problem
Because the guests like to read the log book
So that nobody has to talk to the supervisor

questions.stem: The same toilet in a villa blocks every week. What is the best long-term action?
options: Unblock it each week and say nothing
Lock the bathroom so that no one uses it
Report it so that the cause is found and fixed
Put up a sign asking guests to use less toilet paper

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of preventing a problem before it happens?
options: Waiting for guests to report a broken light
Fixing a leak after the ceiling has fallen in
Checking the bar stock before a busy weekend
Calling a plumber once the room has flooded

questions.stem: After a problem has been solved, what is a good thing to do?
options: Forget about it, since it is over now
Share what was learned with the team
Keep it secret in case you are blamed
Tell the guests every detail of it

questions.stem: Which of these problems at an attraction must be reported at once?
options: A tablecloth has a small coffee stain
A light bulb in the store room is a bit dim
One of the menus has a small tear at one corner
A guest feels faint at the waterfall lookout

questions.stem: Where should you look first for the steps to follow for a common problem at work?
options: The procedures manual for your department
A post on social media from another hotel
A guest's opinion on what should be done
Whatever a friend at another job told you

questions.stem: The housekeeping store at a hotel runs out of toilet rolls on a Sunday, when the supplier is closed. What is the best action?
options: Leave the rooms without toilet rolls until Monday
Buy some with your own money and charge the guests
Take rolls from the staff toilets without telling anyone
Tell the supervisor so stock can be found elsewhere

questions.stem: A small child is missing at a busy attraction, and the parent is very upset. What should staff do first?
options: Tell the parent to wait at the gate until closing time
Follow the lost-child procedure and alert staff at once
Ask the parent why they did not watch the child
Announce it only if the child is not found by evening

questions.stem: A storm warning is given for the parish. What should villa staff do to prevent problems?
options: Wait until the storm arrives and then decide
Leave the pool furniture out so it is easy to use after
Tell guests there is nothing to worry about
Follow the storm plan and secure loose items

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: In a hotel, what do the letters SOP stand for?
What two-word term means the main reason a problem happens, which must be fixed to stop it coming back?
What is the name of the method of asking "Why?" again and again until you reach the real cause of a problem?
What do we call a group method of listing as many ideas as possible, quickly, before judging any of them?
What name is given to a back-up plan that is used if the first plan cannot work?
In Jamaica, what number do you call for the fire brigade or an ambulance?
What do we call a person at work who has been trained to give first aid?
What do we call the written report made after an accident or injury at work?
What do we call an event where nobody was hurt, but someone could easily have been?
What is the short name for the sheet that gives the safety, storage and first-aid facts for a cleaning chemical?
What is the book called where staff write down problems and messages for the next shift?
What word describes an agreement where each side gives up a little to settle a problem?
What do we call anything that could cause harm, such as a loose stair rail or a trailing cable?
In one word, what is the last step of solving a problem, when you check whether the solution worked?
What word is used for a sudden, serious problem that puts people in danger and needs action at once?

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would follow to deal with a familiar workplace problem, from first noticing it to checking the result.
essays.modelAnswer: First I notice the problem and make sure everyone is safe. Then I work out clearly what the problem is, and I gather the facts by asking what, where, when, who and how. Next I look for the cause, not just the signs, for example by asking "Why?" several times. I then think of more than one possible solution and compare them for safety, cost, time and the effect on guests. I check whether the solution is within my authority; if it is not, I report it to my supervisor. Once a solution is agreed, I carry it out, following the property's procedures. Afterwards I check that the problem is really fixed. If it is not, I look at it again and try another option. Last, I record what happened in the log book and share what was learned with the team.
markingPoints: Makes the area safe and works out clearly what the problem is
Gathers the facts and looks for the cause, not just the signs
Thinks of more than one option and chooses one that is safe and within own authority, or reports it
Carries out the agreed solution, following the property's procedures
Checks the result, records it and shares what was learned

essays.stem: Explain the difference between dealing with the signs of a problem and dealing with its cause. Use an example from a villa, hotel or restaurant.
essays.modelAnswer: The signs of a problem are what you can see, such as a wet floor. The cause is the reason it happens, such as a leaking pipe. Dealing only with the signs gives a short-term fix: the problem keeps coming back, wastes time and money, and can upset guests. Dealing with the cause stops it happening again. For example, the walk-in chiller at a restaurant is warm every afternoon. Moving the food to another fridge protects it for now, which is right, but it only deals with the sign. To find the cause, staff ask questions: When does it get warm? Is the door left open during deliveries? Is the door seal damaged? If they find that the door is propped open while stock is unloaded, they can fix the cause by changing the delivery routine, and report the seal to maintenance.
markingPoints: Signs are what is seen; the cause is why it happens
Fixing only the signs is short-term and the problem returns
Gives a suitable example from a villa, hotel or restaurant
Shows how asking questions helps to find the cause
Fixing the cause stops the problem coming back

essays.stem: Explain how you would decide whether you can solve a problem yourself or must report it to your supervisor. Give one example of each.
essays.modelAnswer: I ask myself some questions. Is it safe for me to deal with? Is it part of my job role? Do I have the skills, tools and permission? Will it cost money, or need a decision about rules, refunds or other staff? If it is safe, in my role and within my skills, and no money or rule change is needed, I can usually solve it myself, following the procedures. For example, as a room attendant, if a guest needs more towels or a bin is full, I deal with it at once. If a problem is unsafe, outside my skills or needs a manager's decision, I report it quickly with the facts. For example, if a light switch sparks, I stop anyone using it, keep guests away and report it to my supervisor and maintenance. I never try an electrical repair myself.
markingPoints: Checks safety first
Checks whether it is in own job role, skills and authority
Gives a suitable example of a problem they can solve themselves
Gives a suitable example of a problem they must report, with the reason
Reports quickly with the facts; never attempts unsafe or unauthorised work

essays.stem: Describe how you would report a problem to your supervisor, both by speaking and in writing. Say what information you would give.
essays.modelAnswer: I report the problem as soon as I can. Unless it is urgent, I choose a time and place where guests cannot hear. I speak calmly and clearly and keep to the facts, without blaming anyone. I say what the problem is, where it is, when it started or when I noticed it, who is affected, and what I have already done, such as putting out a sign or moving guests away. If I know the likely cause I say so, and I ask what the supervisor wants me to do next. Then I write it in the log book or on the property's maintenance or problem form, with the date, the time, my name and the same facts, so there is a record that can be followed up. If my supervisor is not there, I tell the person in charge of the shift.
markingPoints: Reports promptly and calmly, away from guests unless urgent
Gives what, where, when and who is affected
Says what action has already been taken
Writes it in the log or on the correct form, with date, time and name
Keeps to the facts; tells the person in charge if the supervisor is away

essays.stem: Late at night, a guest at a villa in Negril tells you that the air conditioner in her bedroom has stopped working. The maintenance staff have gone home. Describe how you would respond.
essays.modelAnswer: I listen to the guest, apologise for the trouble and thank her for telling me. With her permission I check the simple things I am allowed to check, such as whether the switch is on, the remote has batteries and it is set to cool. I do not open the unit or touch any wiring. If it still does not work, I follow the villa's procedure and call the supervisor or the maintenance person on call. While we wait, I offer what I can, such as a standing fan, cold water, or another bedroom if one is free and the supervisor agrees. I tell the guest what will happen and roughly when. I write the problem in the log book and fill in a maintenance request so the day team fixes it first thing. Next morning I check that it has been repaired and that the guest is happy.
markingPoints: Listens, apologises and stays calm and polite
Checks only simple things within own role; does not attempt a repair
Contacts the supervisor or on-call maintenance as the procedure says
Offers a short-term solution and tells the guest what will happen
Records it and follows up the next day

essays.stem: On the path from a hotel to the beach, you find a broken wooden step while guests are walking by. Explain what you would do and why.
essays.modelAnswer: This is a safety problem, so I act at once. First I stop guests from using the broken step: I stand by it, warn people and point them to another path if there is one. Then I put out a warning sign or cones, or tape off the area, so it stays safe when I leave. I do not try to repair the step myself unless that is my job and I have the right tools. I report it straight away to my supervisor and to maintenance, saying exactly where it is and how bad it is, and I fill in a maintenance request. If anyone has already fallen, I check them, get a first aider and fill in an incident report. Later I check that the step has been repaired and the signs removed. I act quickly because a fall could injure a guest and harm the hotel's good name.
markingPoints: Acts at once to keep guests away from the hazard
Puts up signs, cones or tape so the area stays safe
Does not attempt a repair outside own role
Reports to the supervisor and maintenance with the exact place, and fills in the form
Gets first aid and makes an incident report if anyone is hurt; checks the repair later

essays.stem: During the dinner rush at a hotel restaurant, the servers keep running out of clean glasses. Describe how the team could work together to solve this problem.
essays.modelAnswer: After service, the supervisor and the team meet and talk about the problem calmly, without blaming anyone. They gather the facts: How many glasses are there? At what time do they run out? How long does the glass washer take? Is anyone in charge of collecting dirty glasses? Then they look for the cause. Perhaps there are too few glasses, or dirty glasses stay on tables too long. The team brainstorms options, such as clearing glasses more often, running the glass washer before service starts, giving one person the job of collecting and polishing glasses at busy times, or asking the manager to order more. They choose the best options, agree who will do what and from when, and try them. After a week they check whether the problem has stopped, and change the plan if it has not.
markingPoints: Team meets calmly, without blame
Gathers the facts and finds the cause
Lists several possible options
Agrees who will do what, and from when
Checks the result later and changes the plan if needed

essays.stem: Explain why it is important to check whether a solution has worked, and describe what you would do if it had not worked.
essays.modelAnswer: Checking the result tells you whether the problem is really fixed. Without a check, the problem may still be there and could upset the next guest, waste money or cause an accident. It also shows the supervisor that the job was done properly. To check, I look at the result myself, for example switching on a repaired light, or checking that a fridge is back to 5 °C or below (or as the Centre's food safety plan says). I also ask the guest or co-worker who was affected whether things are better. If the solution has not worked, I do not hide it. I report it to my supervisor, look at the problem again to find what was missed, and try another option, or ask for help from someone with more skills. I record each step in the log so everyone knows what has been tried.
markingPoints: Checking shows whether the problem is really fixed
Explains what could happen without a check (guests, cost or safety)
Describes a practical way to check the result
If it failed: reports it honestly and looks at the problem again
Tries another option or gets help, and records what was tried

essays.stem: Explain why workplace problems should be recorded, and how records help a property to stop problems happening again.
essays.modelAnswer: A record, such as an entry in the log book or a maintenance request, makes sure the problem is not forgotten and that the next shift knows about it. It shows who reported it, when, and what was done, so it can be followed up and checked. Records also protect staff, because they show that a problem was reported. Over time, the supervisor can read the records and see patterns. For example, if the same villa toilet blocks every week, or the same freezer alarm goes off every Friday, the records will show it. Then the cause can be found and fixed, such as replacing an old pipe or changing a delivery routine. Records also help the manager plan repairs, order stock and train staff where most problems happen. A good record gives the date, time, place, the problem, the action and the result.
markingPoints: The problem is not forgotten and the next shift is told
Shows who did what and when, so it can be followed up
Records show patterns of repeat problems
Patterns help find and fix causes, and plan repairs, stock and training
Says what a good record includes

essays.stem: Describe how you would compare several possible solutions to a problem and choose the best one. Say what you would think about.
essays.modelAnswer: First I list all the possible solutions, perhaps after brainstorming with my team. Then I compare them one by one. The first thing I check is safety: any solution that could harm a guest or a member of staff is ruled out. Next I think about whether it is within my authority and the property's rules, or needs my supervisor's approval. Then I think about the cost, how long it will take, what tools, people or stock are needed, and how it will affect guests. I also ask whether it fixes the cause or only the signs. For example, if breakfast is always late because the bread arrives at 8 a.m., asking the bakery to deliver earlier is better than serving breakfast without bread. I choose the solution that is safe, allowed and practical and suits guests best, and I agree it with my supervisor before I act.
markingPoints: Lists several options first
Rules out anything unsafe
Checks own authority and the rules; gets approval when needed
Considers cost, time, resources and the effect on guests
Prefers a solution that fixes the cause; agrees it before acting

practical1.title: Find, deal with and report familiar problems in a mock villa
practical1.brief: The assessor sets up the Centre's mock villa (bedroom, bathroom, kitchenette and patio) with about eight familiar problems, for example: a wet patch on the floor, boxes blocking an exit, a kettle with a damaged cable, an empty soap dispenser, a bedside lamp that does not work, a dripping tap, a stained towel, and a guest's note asking for a late check-out. As a group, walk through the villa with the problem list and find every problem. Share the work: each member leads on at least two problems and decides, with the group, whether it is within a room attendant's role to fix or must be reported. Fix the ones you are allowed to fix (for example, put out a wet floor sign and dry the floor, clear the exit, change the towel and refill the soap). For the others, make the area safe, tag faulty items "Do not use", fill in a maintenance request or a log book entry, and report the problem by speaking to the "supervisor" (the assessor). Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the completed forms to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: The Centre's mock villa, set up by the assessor with about 8 problems
A problem list sheet and a clipboard for the group
Wet floor sign, mop, bucket, cloths and gloves
Blank maintenance request forms and a log book page
photos: The group starting the walk-through with the problem list
Each problem as it was found (one photo each)
A problem fixed within the group's role, such as the wet floor sign out and the floor dried
A faulty item tagged "Do not use" and set aside
A member reporting a problem to the "supervisor"
The villa after every problem was dealt with
checklist: Looked carefully and checked each area, finding the problems they led on
Made each hazard safe at once (sign, tag, cleared exit) before moving on
Decided correctly which problems were within their role and which must be reported
Did not attempt any electrical or plumbing repair
Fixed in-role problems to the property's standard
Reported clearly to the supervisor: what, where, when and what had been done
Completed a maintenance request or log entry fully and clearly
Worked with the group and shared the tasks fairly
safety: Never touch the inside of an electrical item or a damaged cable. Switch off at the wall and unplug only if the assessor allows it, then tag it "Do not use"
Put out the wet floor sign before mopping, and wear gloves
Lift boxes safely: bend the knees, keep the back straight and get help with heavy loads
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for any cleaning product
Use only made-up guest names and details

practical2.title: Solve a repeat problem as a team: find the cause and make an action plan
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a case file from a hotel in Montego Bay: two weeks of log book entries, guest comment cards and a staff schedule, which all point to one repeat problem (for example, rooms not ready by check-in time, or breakfast tables not set when the restaurant opens). As a group: (1) write the problem in one clear sentence on a flip chart; (2) list the facts from the file (what, where, when, who and how often); (3) find the root cause using the "5 whys", writing each "why" on the chart; (4) brainstorm at least four possible solutions and compare them in a table for safety, cost, time and the effect on guests; (5) choose the best solution and write an action plan that says who will do what, by when, and how the result will be checked; (6) present the plan to the "manager" (the assessor) in about 10 minutes. Share the parts so that every member leads at least one step and every member presents part of the plan. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, the table and the action plan to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A case file from the assessor (log entries, comment cards and a staff schedule)
Flip chart paper, a stand, markers and tape
Blank comparison table and action plan forms
A phone or tablet for the photos
photos: The problem statement and the list of facts on the flip chart
The "5 whys" chain on the flip chart
The brainstorm list of possible solutions
Each member presenting their part to the "manager"
checklist: Took part in reading the case file and picking out the facts
Helped write the problem clearly in one sentence
Helped find the cause, not just the signs, using the 5 whys
Offered at least one possible solution in the brainstorm
Compared the solutions for safety, cost, time and effect on guests
Helped write an action plan with tasks, names, dates and a check
Presented their part clearly and answered the manager's questions
Listened to others and respected their ideas
safety: Keep the work area tidy, with bags and cables out of the walkways
Set the flip chart stand on level floor so it cannot tip over
Take a short break and drink water during the 3 hours
Use only the made-up names in the case file; never use real guests' or staff members' details
